notes: 495 findings extracted from 10 cells; 494 clustered into 26 clusters; 1 excluded (anthropic-code-review r2 candidate the tool itself rejected/scored 0 in its own output — never asserted). Blind grading: clusters shuffled (seed 42), tool identity stripped.

primary_bug.summary: The rewrite loses the old 'searched, not found' sentinel, making the re-added Debug.Assert a wrong invariant that terminates debug-build processes. Old code initialized `_rowidOrdinal = -1` before the scan, so `Debug.Assert(_rowidOrdinal.HasValue)` was vacuously true and the not-found case flowed to the `< 0` MemoryStream fallback. New code leaves `rowIdForOrdinal` null when the scan finds no rowid column for the blob's (database, table) — expression columns with no backing table (e.g. `SELECT 'test'`), queries that don't select the table's INTEGER PK/rowid, composite-PK or WITHOUT ROWID tables — and then `Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal != null)` FIRES, killing the process in Debug builds (xUnit run: 'Process terminated. Assertion failed.' at SqliteDataRecord.cs:393, test GetFieldValue_of_TextReader_works doing `SELECT 'test'`, via GetTextReader → GetStream). In Release the assert compiles out and the null correctly falls back to MemoryStream, so the defect is the assertion itself asserting a state that is legitimately reachable.
primary_bug.locus: GetStream ~L326-395: `if (!RowIds.TryGetValue(rowidkey, out rowIdForOrdinal)) { ...scan... Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null); }` — the assert after the scan loop.
primary_bug.must_flag: A reviewer catches the primary bug if it flags that `Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal != null)` can fire — i.e., that 'no rowid column found' is a legitimate, reachable outcome of the scan (expression/computed columns with no table, PK not in the select list, WITHOUT ROWID or composite-PK tables) and the new code asserts it cannot happen, crashing Debug builds / the test suite, whereas the old `-1` sentinel encoded not-found as a valid asserted state. Equivalent formulations count: 'the assert is no longer vacuously true / the invariant is wrong', 'null is a legal post-loop state so the assert will fail on non-table columns', 'Debug.Assert semantics changed from HasValue (always true) to found (not always true)'. Merely noting the null-fallback branch exists, or that the not-found result is never cached (perf), does NOT count — the crash-on-assert facet must be named.
primary_bug.source: revert PR #32945 ('Revert ... due to test failures', reverts merge 9e69b85) + regression issue #32944 (stack: Process terminated, Assertion failed at SqliteDataRecord.cs:393 in GetStream, from GetFieldValue_of_TextReader_works). Verified against the checkout at the merge SHA: the failing test runs `SELECT 'test';` — single expression column, scan loop skips i==ordinal, ends with rowIdForOrdinal == null, assert fires.
primary_bug.difficulty: moderate — the assert is visibly reachable from the diff alone (the null-check fallback two lines below it admits null is possible, so the assert and the fallback contradict each other). But it hides in plain sight: ErikEJ's review comment 'Re-add Assert' caused the author to re-add it, and maintainers merged it. A reviewer must reason about what the loop guarantees rather than trust the assert.

human_issues.summary: ajcvickers: 'Any reason not to use a value tuple for this?' — the RowIdInfo nested class (mutable, public setters, TableName never read) could be a value tuple/record; author answered 'It was only for readability' and kept the class. Live minor style/design point against the final diff: a cluster suggesting RowIdInfo be a tuple/record/readonly struct, or noting its TableName field is never used, matches this.
human_issues.thread: PR 32770 review comment by ajcvickers at SqliteDataRecord.cs:20: 'Any reason not to use a value tuple for this?' / author: 'It was only for readability'

known_safe.summary: The `if (rowIdForOrdinal == null) return new MemoryStream(GetCachedBlob(ordinal), false);` branch means there is NO null-dereference at `rowIdForOrdinal.Ordinal` — claiming an NRE on the later use is refuted; null is checked before use. (The defect is the Debug.Assert above it, not a missing null check below.)

The scan loop DOES filter candidate columns by database name and table name (pre-existing `if (databaseName != blobDatabaseName) continue;` and `if (tableName != blobTableName) continue;` lines, unchanged by the diff) before the rowid/PK checks — claiming 'another table's rowid/PK could be picked for this blob' is refuted. The pkColumns memoization is also safe: every column reaching it belongs to blobTableName.

RowIds is a readonly INSTANCE field on SqliteDataRecord (one per query execution), not static — claims of cross-query cache poisoning, unbounded growth across statements, or thread-shared state are refuted. It lives and dies with the data record.

clusters.summary: Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal != null) after the scan loop asserts a false invariant: 'no rowid found for the blob's (database, table)' is a legitimate, reachable outcome (expression columns with no table, PK not selected, composite-PK / WITHOUT ROWID tables) that the null-check fallback two lines below explicitly handles, so the assert fires and terminates the process in Debug builds; the old code's -1 sentinel made the equivalent assert vacuously true.
clusters.rationale: Meets every must_flag facet: names the assert (line 393) firing and terminating the process in Debug builds, identifies 'no rowid found' as a legitimate reachable scan outcome (expression columns, unselected PK, composite-PK/WITHOUT ROWID), notes the contradiction with the null fallback two lines below, and contrasts with the old -1 sentinel that made the assert vacuously true. This is the defect that got the PR reverted (#32945, issue #32944).

clusters.summary: The 'searched, not found' outcome is never stored in the RowIds dictionary (only found branches call Add), so every subsequent GetStream/GetBytes/GetChars/GetTextReader call on a no-rowid table re-runs the full O(FieldCount) metadata scan plus a fresh pragma_table_info SQL query — a regression vs. the old -1 sentinel which memoized the negative result.
clusters.rationale: Verified: RowIds.Add appears only in the two found branches (lines 355, 387), so a not-found (db,table) is rescanned on every GetStream — and GetBytes calls GetStream per call (line 276), so chunked reads on a no-rowid column repeat the O(FieldCount) metadata scan and can re-run the pragma_table_info query (line 377) each time; the old code memoized not-found as -1 once per record. Real Release-build perf/behavior regression distinct from the assert crash.

clusters.summary: The cache key $"{blobDatabaseName}_{blobTableName}" is built by naive '_' concatenation and is not injective — distinct (database, table) pairs whose names contain underscores (e.g. ATTACHed databases) can collide, silently reusing the wrong table's cached rowid ordinal (wrong row's blob bytes or a spurious error).
clusters.rationale: True in principle: $"{db}_{table}" (line 328) is not injective when names contain underscores (requires ATTACHed databases with adversarial names plus blob reads from both colliding pairs in one query — contrived), and a collision would reuse the wrong table's cached ordinal. One-shot fix (tuple key), but the scenario is remote; valid-minor at best.

clusters.summary: Self-join: sqlite3_column_table_name returns the origin table name, not the SQL alias, so two aliases of the same table share one cache key and the second alias's blob is resolved with the first alias's rowid ordinal — silently the wrong row's blob; the PR's per-table fix does not cover this degenerate case (pre-existing in kind) and no test exercises it.
clusters.rationale: Verified mechanics: sqlite3_column_table_name yields the origin table for both aliases of a self-join, so both VALUE columns share key 'main_A'; the first read caches the first alias's PK ordinal (via the pkColumns==1 path) and the second alias's blob is opened with the first alias's rowid — silently wrong bytes. Pre-existing in kind (the old single _rowidOrdinal failed the same way), but self-joins sit squarely inside this PR's stated multi-blob-JOIN purpose, so a maintainer reviewing it should know the fix's boundary.

clusters.summary: The RowIdInfo nested class is over-designed: TableName is assigned at both construction sites but never read (dead state), both properties have public setters though set exactly once, internal visibility is wider than needed, and the type reduces to an int (or a tuple/record per repo idiom).
clusters.rationale: Matches h1 exactly: RowIdInfo (lines 20-30) has TableName assigned at both construction sites (354, 386) but never read, mutable public setters set exactly once, and reduces to an int/tuple — ajcvickers' live review comment ('Any reason not to use a value tuple for this?') is precisely this finding.

clusters.summary: The new RowIds field violates the file's field conventions: PascalCase with no explicit access modifier where every sibling private field is 'private' + _camelCase (per .editorconfig).
clusters.rationale: Verified: all 12 sibling private fields in the file are 'private _camelCase'; RowIds (line 39) is PascalCase with no access modifier, violating dotnet_style_require_accessibility_modifiers = always (.editorconfig line 59) and the file's uniform field convention (the _camelCase naming style is defined at .editorconfig 194-195). One-shot, anchored fix.

clusters.summary: Local variable 'rowidkey' is an unbroken lowercase run, deviating from the camelCase convention of every other multi-word local in the method (should be rowIdKey, and var per file usage).
clusters.rationale: Verified: 'rowidkey' sits beside rowIdForOrdinal/blobDatabaseName/pkColumns in the same method; .editorconfig binds locals to camel_case_style (everything_else_naming) and csharp_style_var_for_built_in_types = true (line 88) makes the explicit 'string' also off-idiom. One-shot rename anchored in file + .editorconfig conventions.

clusters.summary: Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null) is missing spaces around the != operator, contrary to the .editorconfig binary-operator spacing rule.
clusters.rationale: Verified: line 393 reads 'rowIdForOrdinal!=null' and .editorconfig line 157 sets csharp_space_around_binary_operators = before_and_after. Direct, one-shot, .editorconfig-anchored violation.

clusters.summary: RowIdInfo? rowIdForOrdinal = null; is a redundant pre-declaration before the TryGetValue out argument — the codebase idiom is inline 'out var'.
clusters.rationale: Verified: lines 327-329 pre-declare and null-initialize before TryGetValue assigns via out; the file itself uses inline 'out var' (line 150, lines 364-368) and .editorconfig line 106 sets csharp_style_inlined_variable_declaration = true. The out-var form remains in scope for the later null check, so the rewrite is a safe one-shot fix.

clusters.summary: Whitespace churn introduced by the diff: a stray whitespace-only line after the namespace opening brace, a stray blank line splitting the field block, and a removed blank line after 'var pkColumns = -1L;' (trim_trailing_whitespace violations).
clusters.rationale: Verified: SqliteDataRecord.cs:17 is a whitespace-only line with 4 trailing spaces (cat -A shows '    $'), violating .editorconfig's trim_trailing_whitespace = true (line 10); the stray blank line after RowIds and the removed blank after pkColumns are also in the diff. Anchored in .editorconfig, one-shot, converges.

clusters.summary: The new test verifies the joined non-blob columns only via Console.WriteLine — xUnit does not capture console output and nothing is asserted, so wrong GetInt32 values would pass silently; should be Assert.Equal.
clusters.rationale: Verified at test line 171: the GetInt32 results go only to Console.WriteLine (xUnit does not capture Console), so wrong join values would pass; the accompanying comment states intent to verify these reads. Sibling tests assert values (e.g. lines 114-115). One-shot Assert.Equal fix anchored in sibling idiom.

clusters.summary: The new test discards the GetBytes return values instead of asserting them (sibling tests assert the returned count).
clusters.rationale: Verified: sibling tests assert the GetBytes return count (lines 114-115, 198-200, 218-219) while the new test discards both return values (lines 175, 179). One-shot addition anchored in the file's own convention.

clusters.summary: The new test's comments are defective: '//this was failing. now should be fixed' narrates change history, '//get len of abuff' misdescribes the adjacent code (nothing obtains a length), the '//reading fields...' comment has a grammar error, and the test lacks the file's '[Fact] // Issue #NNNNN' provenance idiom.
clusters.rationale: Verified: '//get len of abuff' (test line 173) objectively misdescribes the adjacent code (GetBytes reads bytes, nothing obtains a length), and '//this was failing. now should be fixed' narrates change history; the '[Fact] // Issue #NNNNN' idiom exists at lines 2264/2321. Objective comment incorrectness is a one-shot, in-repo-anchored fix.

clusters.summary: Test-coverage gaps around the new caching mechanism: no join-with-fallback-table case, no reverse/interleaved read order, no multi-row iteration over the cached path, no ATTACH/database-name coverage, no WITHOUT ROWID or aliased-rowid-projection cases, no single-row pin — the new test covers only the happy two-table path.
clusters.rationale: An open-ended 'more tests' list (six-plus scenarios: fallback-in-join, read order, multi-row, ATTACH, WITHOUT ROWID, aliased projection) — exactly the unbounded suggestion class the rubric defaults to trivia; it never names the assert-crash consequence that would have elevated the not-found-path item.

clusters.summary: The dictionary cache-hit branch (TryGetValue returning true) is executed by zero tests — a wrong stored ordinal or stale entry would be invisible to the suite.
clusters.rationale: Verified across the component's test suite: the only tests calling GetStream twice on one record (GetStream_works and the _with_text/_int/_float variants) use expression columns whose not-found result is never cached, and every table-backed test (GetStream_Blob_works, _when_long_pk, _composite_pk_and_rowid, GetBytes/GetChars/GetTextReader streaming, the new JOIN test) makes exactly one read per key — so TryGetValue never returns true. A targeted, bounded test for the PR's core mechanism.

clusters.summary: The new test asserts only byte content and never the stream type, so it cannot distinguish true SqliteBlob streaming from the MemoryStream fallback — a silent regression to the buffered path would still pass; sibling tests use Assert.IsType<SqliteBlob>.
clusters.rationale: Verified: sibling GetStream tests assert the stream type (Assert.IsType<SqliteBlob> at lines 478, 505, 561; IsType<MemoryStream> at 385, 533), while the new test named 'works_streaming_join' asserts only bytes via GetBytes — a regression to the MemoryStream fallback would return identical bytes and pass. One-shot fix anchored in sibling idiom.

clusters.summary: The new caching scheme is undocumented: the RowIds key format (underscore join, null-name sentinel), the cache's changed semantics (only successes cached), and RowIdInfo's purpose carry no comments despite the file's // NB: idiom.
clusters.rationale: The file's '// NB:' comments (SqliteDataRecord.cs:111,129,177,308,485) are a narrow 'message provided by framework' idiom, not a documentation-density convention; demanding comments for the key format/cache semantics is taste-level doc appetite with no in-repo anchor, and maintainers merged without requesting any.

clusters.summary: RowIdInfo.TableName is declared non-nullable string but is assigned from sqlite3_column_table_name(...).utf8_to_string(), which the same file treats as nullable and which returns null for expression columns — the annotation is unenforced.
clusters.rationale: The premise checks out (the file treats utf8_to_string() as nullable at lines 126 and 184; TableName is declared non-nullable string), but at both construction sites tableName is provably non-null in practice (columnName == "rowid" implies a table-backed column; the metadata call would throw first), and TableName is never read anyway — an unenforced annotation with zero behavioral consequence.

clusters.summary: The RowIds dictionary is eagerly allocated in every SqliteDataRecord construction, unlike every sibling cache in the class which is nullable and lazily initialized.
clusters.rationale: Verified: every sibling cache in the field block (_blobCache, _typeCache, _columnNameOrdinalCache, _columnNameCache, lines 34-37) is nullable and lazily initialized, while RowIds (line 39) allocates a Dictionary in every data-record construction even when no blob is ever read. Mechanical one-shot fix anchored in the adjacent convention.

clusters.summary: A new interpolated key string is allocated on every GetStream call, including cache hits (per chunk during chunked blob reads), where the pre-change code did a zero-allocation check.
clusters.rationale: True (line 328 allocates the interpolated key on every GetStream, and GetBytes calls GetStream per call at line 276), but the same path already allocates two utf8_to_string strings (lines 324-325, pre-existing) and opens a SqliteBlob per chunk; the added allocation is a micro-optimization with no meaningful consequence and no one-shot fix short of restructuring the key.

clusters.summary: Under multithreaded misuse (outside DbDataReader's contract) RowIds.Add can throw ArgumentException on a duplicate key or corrupt the dictionary, where the old int? field raced benignly; the indexer would be idempotent.
clusters.rationale: Self-conceded to be outside DbDataReader's documented single-threaded contract; RowIds is an instance field scoped to one query execution (answer-key known_safe confirms no shared state), so the duplicate-key Add throw requires misuse with no concrete in-contract pathway — speculative hardening.

clusters.summary: Test formatting drift: trailing whitespace inside the verbatim SQL literal, multi-line SQL diverging from the file's compact single-line convention, a stray blank line before the closing brace, and abuff/bbuff naming vs the sibling 'buffer' convention.
clusters.rationale: Verified: test lines 158 and 163 end in trailing whitespace inside the verbatim SQL, violating trim_trailing_whitespace = true (.editorconfig line 10); the stray blank line before the closing brace (line 181) and abuff/bbuff vs the sibling 'buffer' convention are also real. Anchored, one-shot cleanup, though the multi-line-SQL item is taste.

clusters.summary: The choice B.ID=1000 in the new test is load-bearing (had B.ID been 1, the stale-rowid bug would coincidentally pass) and is documented nowhere in the test.
clusters.rationale: The observation is correct (with B.ID=1, the old stale-rowid code would open B's row 1 and coincidentally return correct bytes; B.ID=1000 forces the failure), but the ask is a missing explanatory comment guarding a hypothetical future edit — meta test-design commentary, not an incorrect artifact; no in-repo anchor compels it.

clusters.summary: Pre-existing, adjacent to the diff: the pragma_table_info($table) query is not schema-qualified, so it resolves against schema search order rather than the column's databaseName — an ATTACHed table sharing a name with a main table can yield a wrong pkColumns count.
clusters.rationale: The pragma_table_info($table) query (line 377) is pre-existing context, unchanged by the diff, and the ATTACH same-name collision scenario is contrived; the diff does not make it worse (the old code cached the resulting ordinal for the same record lifetime). Pre-existing and outside the PR's change surface.

clusters.summary: Pre-existing, adjacent to the diff: a single-column INTEGER PK on a WITHOUT ROWID table satisfies the pkColumns==1 branch and is treated as a rowid alias, but sqlite3_blob_open would fail at runtime; untested.
clusters.rationale: True in principle (a WITHOUT ROWID table's single INTEGER PK satisfies the pkColumns==1 branch and sqlite3_blob_open cannot open WITHOUT ROWID tables), but the detection logic is pre-existing — the diff only changed what gets assigned in that branch, not the classification — and the scenario is orthogonal to the PR's per-table-caching purpose.

clusters.summary: Expression/computed blob columns (empty database/table name) all map to the sentinel key '_'; two expression-derived blob columns would share one cache entry — unexercised by tests.
clusters.rationale: The claimed shared cache entry cannot exist: RowIds.Add is only called in the two found branches (lines 355, 387), and no entry can ever be created under the '_' key because expression columns have null origin names (never == "rowid") and the metadata path cannot yield a PK match for a null table. Not-found is never cached, so each expression blob column independently falls to the MemoryStream branch; nothing is shared.
